subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: The Filter Bubble
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Filter Bubble usable.

hook.text: Two people search the same term on Google. They get completely different results.

buildup.text: Algorithms personalize your feed based on past clicks, creating a bubble of familiar content.

discovery.text: Eli Pariser coined 'filter bubble' in 2011, warning that personalization narrows what we see.

twist.text: You think you're exploring the internet. The internet is showing you a carefully curated slice.

climax.text: Filter bubbles don't just shape shopping. They shape political beliefs, worldviews, and reality itself.

punchline.text: The internet you see is built just for you. That's the problem.

quiz.question: What is a filter bubble?
options: Personalized content that narrows your exposure to diverse viewpoints
A spam filter that blocks unwanted emails
A privacy tool that hides your browsing
